def schedule(tasks, capacity):
    if not tasks:
        return {"jobs": [], "makespan": 0}
    
    # Build lookup
    task_map = {}
    for t in tasks:
        task_map[t["id"]] = t
    
    # Validate units > capacity
    for t in tasks:
        if t["units"] > capacity:
            raise ValueError("units exceeds capacity")
    
    # Validate unknown deps
    for t in tasks:
        for d in t["deps"]:
            if d not in task_map:
                raise ValueError("unknown dependency")
    
    # Validate no circular dependency (topological sort / DFS)
    # Use DFS with coloring
    WHITE, GRAY, BLACK = 0, 1, 2
    color = {t["id"]: WHITE for t in tasks}
    
    def dfs(node):
        color[node] = GRAY
        for d in task_map[node]["deps"]:
            if color[d] == GRAY:
                raise ValueError("circular dependency")
            if color[d] == WHITE:
                dfs(d)
        color[node] = BLACK
    
    for t in tasks:
        if color[t["id"]] == WHITE:
            dfs(t["id"])
    
    # Simulation
    all_ids = sorted(task_map.keys())
    completed = set()
    started = set()
    running = {}  # id -> end_time
    available = capacity
    t = 0
    jobs = []
    
    while len(completed) < len(tasks):
        # Release completed tasks
        newly_completed = [tid for tid, end in running.items() if end <= t]
        for tid in newly_completed:
            completed.add(tid)
            available += task_map[tid]["units"]
            del running[tid]
        
        # Scan tasks in lexicographic order
        for tid in all_ids:
            if tid in started:
                continue
            # Check deps
            if all(d in completed for d in task_map[tid]["deps"]):
                if available >= task_map[tid]["units"]:
                    # Start this task
                    started.add(tid)
                    available -= task_map[tid]["units"]
                    end_time = t + task_map[tid]["duration"]
                    running[tid] = end_time
                    jobs.append({"id": tid, "start": t, "end": end_time})
        
        # Advance to earliest running task end
        if running:
            t = min(running.values())
        else:
            # No running tasks and not all completed - shouldn't happen with valid input
            # But just in case, break to avoid infinite loop
            break
    
    makespan = max(j["end"] for j in jobs) if jobs else 0
    
    # Sort jobs by id
    jobs.sort(key=lambda x: x["id"])
    
    return {"jobs": jobs, "makespan": makespan}
